newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia's CPI rose 0.8 pct in November.
newsitem.headline: Colombia's CPI rose 0.8 pct in November.

text.p: Colombia's consumer price index rose a lower-than-expected 0.8 percent in November, the National Statistics Department (DANE) said.

As measured on an accumulated basis for the first 11 months of the year, it said the index had now risen 20.76 percent, well above the 17 percent target the central bank had originally set for all of 1996.

The bank and finance ministry announced Friday that it had set an 18 percent inflation target for 1997 but this could be difficult to achieve due to an expected wave of price hikes early next year caused by a sharp rise in electricity rates.

The rise in the CPI in November compares with a 0.79 percent percent increase in the same month last year. Real inflation this year is expected to be close to 22 percent, according to most independent analysts.
Inflation over the past 12 months now stands at 21.88 percent, according to figures released by DANE.
This compares with a 20.13 percent increase between November 1994 and November 1995.
